# 08 — Manifest V3 & Chrome Web Store Compliance

Goal: pass review fast and stay listed. Every item here is a hard requirement.

## 1. Manifest (generated by WXT from `wxt.config.ts`)

```ts
export default defineConfig({
  modules: ['@wxt-dev/module-svelte'],
  manifest: {
    name: '__MSG_appName__',
    description: '__MSG_appDesc__',
    default_locale: 'en',
    minimum_chrome_version: String(CHROME_FLOOR),   // 136 — the ES2025 floor, 01 §1
    permissions: ['bookmarks', 'storage'],   // ← the complete list, forever (v1)
    action: { default_popup: 'popup.html' }, // WXT wires this automatically
    options_ui: { page: 'manager.html#settings', open_in_tab: true },
    // NO host_permissions, NO content_scripts, NO background
  },
});
```

## 2. Permissions — justification table (paste into CWS review notes)

| Permission | Justification (single purpose) |
|---|---|
| `bookmarks` | Core feature: read the bookmark tree for export/editing; create/move/update/remove nodes for import/editing. |
| `storage` | Persist user settings (language, theme, defaults) and legal-acceptance flag locally. No user content stored. |

**Forbidden without a doc update + review:** `tabs`, `downloads`,
`host_permissions`, `activeTab`, `scripting`, `alarms`. The design
deliberately avoids each (see `01_TECH_STACK.md §3`, `02_ARCHITECTURE.md §6`).

## 3. Code integrity rules

- **No remotely hosted code.** All JS/CSS ships in the package. No CDN
  `<script>`, no `import()` of URLs, no `eval`, no `new Function`, no string
  `setTimeout`. The extension-page CSP (below) enforces this, and Chrome
  rejects any manifest that loosens the MV3 minimum.
- **No runtime network requests at all** (stronger than required): no network
  calls, no remote favicons, no update pings. Three layers enforce it since
  v1.1.0 — the browser, a build gate and a source gate:

#### Layer 1 — the extension-page CSP (browser-enforced)

MV3's default extension CSP (`script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval';
object-src 'self';`) restricts code execution only; it has no `connect-src` or
`img-src` at all. Until v1.0.1 that left a grep gate as the *only* thing between
the product and its zero-network claim. The production manifest now declares:

```
script-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; connect-src 'none'; img-src 'self' data: blob:;
style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; font-src 'self'; media-src 'none'; frame-src 'none';
worker-src 'self'; form-action 'none'; base-uri 'none'
```

`connect-src 'none'` makes Chrome refuse every fetch, XHR, WebSocket,
EventSource and beacon from an extension page; the rest closes remote images,
stylesheets, fonts, media, frames and form posts. `style-src` keeps
`'unsafe-inline'` because Svelte sets `style` attributes; there is **no
`default-src`**, on purpose, because it would govern every unlisted directive. User-initiated
navigation — an About link, or "Open" on a bookmark via `tabs.create` — is not
governed by a page CSP and is not a request the extension makes (`09 §1`).

- **The rule is: only ever tighten.** Adding `'unsafe-*'`, a remote source, or
  removing a directive is a security regression, and `check:manifest` fails on
  any string other than the exact one above.
- **Production builds only.** `wxt.config.ts` emits it when the command is
  `build` (so `npm run build` and `npm run zip`), because the dev server reloads
  the extension over a localhost websocket that `connect-src 'none'` blocks.
- Vite's modulepreload polyfill is disabled (`modulePreload.polyfill: false`):
  it was the one network call in the shipped bundle, dead code for every Chrome
  at the floor.

#### Layer 2 — the built-artifact gate

`npm run check:manifest` (`scripts/check-manifest.mjs`) scans every `.js` file
in `.output/chrome-mv3` for network APIs — including code that arrived through
a dependency, which no source gate can see — and pins the manifest: MV3, the
permission list, the exact key set, the Chrome floor, the exact CSP, and that
every file the manifest and pages reference exists.

#### Layer 3 — the source gate

`npm run guard` (`scripts/guard.mjs`). **The rule set lives in that file, not
here** — this section used to restate it, and the copy drifted (its `\{@html\}`
matched only the literal `{@html}`). The script header explains each rule and
`tests/unit/scripts/guard.test.ts` holds a passing and a failing case for every
one, including the bypasses an audit found against the old line-by-line regexes
(aliases, computed global access, multi-line calls, `+=`, `{ @html }`, remote
`url()` in CSS, resource hints). It scans `src/**` — `.ts`, `.svelte`, `.html`,
`.css` and friends — with no exemptions, matches across line breaks, and fails
if it scanned nothing. Because identifiers are banned outright, the bare API
names cannot appear in `src/` comments either; write "network call".

- **Minification: yes. Obfuscation: NO.** CWS has prohibited obfuscated code
  since 2018; WXT/Vite default minify (whitespace/identifier shortening) is
  allowed and sufficient. Never add an obfuscator plugin. Open-source repo +
  readable build = faster review.

## 4. Single purpose statement (CWS "single purpose" field)

> Import, export, and edit browser bookmarks and bookmark folder trees using
> local files, entirely offline.

Everything in the UI must map to that sentence. (This is why dead-link
checking is out of scope — it changes the permission story.)

## 5. Privacy tab answers (CWS Dashboard)

| Dashboard question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Does your extension collect user data? | **No** — for every category (PII, health, financial, auth, personal communications, location, web history, user activity, website content). |
| Data usage certifications | Certify: no sale, no unrelated use, no creditworthiness use. |
| Privacy policy URL | `https://github.com/poli0981/bookmarkmagic/blob/main/legal/PRIVACY.md` — **required, not optional**: CWS mandates a posted policy even for extensions that only handle data locally |
| Remote code | **No** |

Note: nothing is collected, stored off-device, or transmitted — there is no
server and no network call — so "No collection" is the accurate answer on the
data-usage checkboxes. That is *not* the same as being exempt from disclosure:
CWS requires extensions to describe how they handle user data **even when the
handling is entirely local**, which is why the privacy-policy URL above is
mandatory and why `legal/PRIVACY.md` spells out the local bookmark reads/writes
and the `chrome.storage.local` settings explicitly (`14 §3`).

The single-purpose text (§4) and the per-permission justifications (§2) are
also submitted on this tab — keep all three in sync, and re-certify whenever
any of them changes (`09 §4`).

## 6. Store listing compliance

- Final name **BookmarkMagic** makes no sync claim — no cloud-syncing
  implication for reviewers. The description still leads with "offline, no
  account, no cloud" to set user expectations.
- No keyword stuffing in the description; functionality claims must all be
  real at submission time.
- Screenshots must show the actual extension UI (see `13_RELEASE_PUBLISHING.md`).
- Category: **Productivity → Tools** (align with dashboard's current taxonomy
  at submission ⚠️).

## 7. MV3 technical notes

- MV2 is fully retired; WXT builds MV3 for Chromium by default — never set
  `manifest_version: 2` for the Chrome target.
- No background service worker is registered at all (§02). If one ever
  becomes necessary, it must be an ES module (`type: 'module'`) and
  event-driven only.
- Extension pages (popup/manager) may use `DOMParser`, `Blob`, `<a download>`
  freely — these need no permissions.
- **The floor is Chrome 136** (`minimum_chrome_version: "136"`, since v1.1.0;
  120 before). It is set by the language, not by an extension API: 136 is the
  first Chrome with every ES2025 built-in, and tsconfig's `lib` is ES2025
  (`01 §1`). The highest extension-API floors are far below it —
  `browser.runtime.getContexts()` needs 116 and `scheduler.yield()` 129 — so
  `scheduler.yield()` is in fact always present. The write queue still keeps
  its nullish fallback (`05 §6`) because the test environment has no
  `scheduler`; it only works if written with explicit parentheses, see the
  warning there.
- Raising the floor is a **user-visible** event even though it is not a
  permission change: a user below it keeps the installed version and simply
  stops receiving updates. Say so in the CHANGELOG, and never raise it in a
  patch release.

## 8. Review-readiness checklist (before every submission)

- [ ] `npm run verify` green; `wxt zip` output installs cleanly via
      "Load unpacked" on a fresh profile.
- [ ] Manifest diff reviewed — permission list unchanged (`bookmarks`,
      `storage` only).
- [ ] `npm run guard` and `npm run check:manifest` pass (§3: the source gate,
      and the built-artifact gate that pins the CSP and scans the bundle). Note
      `{@html}` is **not** catchable by Biome — no such rule exists for Svelte —
      so the source gate plus review is its whole enforcement.
- [ ] Right-click → Options lands on `#settings` both on a fresh profile and
      with a Manager tab already open on another route (§1 uses an undocumented
      URL fragment; `02 §5`).
- [ ] All three `_locales` load (chrome://extensions shows localized name
      when browser language switched).
- [ ] Version bumped (semver) in `package.json` (WXT propagates to manifest).
- [ ] Privacy tab answers unchanged, or updated + re-certified.
- [ ] Store listing screenshots regenerated if the UI changed.
